strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local compute (abs, mean, scale) between each. Dispatches 8 all-reduces total. Represents the naive approach with maximum dispatch count but simplest logic—no optimization, just faithful iteration of the dependent computation pattern.

strategies.name: Fused Local Computation Per Iteration
strategies.desc: Merges all per-block local operations (abs, mean, multiply, divide) into single vectorized kernels before/after each all-reduce to minimize graph fragmentation. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces intermediate tensor allocations and potential XLA recompilations. Trades code complexity for better memory locality and fewer local-op dispatches.

strategies.name: Batched All-Reduce with Metadata Encoding
strategies.desc: Encodes scaling factors as auxiliary channels or concatenated metadata tensors, performing fewer all-reduces (e.g., 4 instead of 8) by batching pairs of dependent iterations and unpacking results. Reduces all-reduce dispatch count by ~50% at cost of increased payload size and local unpacking overhead.

strategies.name: Pipelined Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing computation on partial results during the scatter phase. Theoretically 16 collective dispatches but enables overlapping communication with local abs/mean computation on scattered chunks. Trades dispatch count for potential latency hiding.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce
strategies.desc:
Exploits multi-node topology (world_size=224 suggests 28 or 32 nodes): first performs intra-node reductions, then inter-node, then broadcasts back. Reduces cross-node traffic by performing local aggregation first. Increases dispatch count per iteration (2-3x) but reduces per-dispatch payload and leverages faster intra-node interconnect.

def r61b_dd_absmean_p512_d8_fn(x, rank, world_size, num_devices,
                 cores_per_device, xm, torch, num_nodes=1):
    S = 512
    B = 8
    dtype = x.dtype
    
    # Initial all-reduce
    s = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, x)
    
    # Reshape for more efficient batch operations
    s_reshaped = s.view(B, S)
    
    # Process iterations 1-6 with batched operations
    for iteration in range(6):
        # Compute all factors at once using vectorized operations
        # abs().mean(dim=1) computes mean for each batch element
        f = 1.0 + s_reshaped.abs().mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)  # Shape: (B, 1)
        
        # Scale all batches at once with broadcasting
        buf = s_reshaped * f
        
        # Single all-reduce for this iteration
        acc = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf.view(-1))
        acc_reshaped = acc.view(B, S)
        
        # Unscale all batches at once
        s_reshaped = acc_reshaped / (world_size * f)
    
    # Final iteration (iteration 7) - no unscaling by factors
    f = 1.0 + s_reshaped.abs().mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    buf = s_reshaped * f
    acc = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf.view(-1))
    acc = acc / world_size
    
    return acc
